# fivenines_proxmox_cluster_nodes (Data Source)

The nodes in one Proxmox cluster, and which of them the cluster can no longer see.

ONE ROW PER ENTITY however many hosts report the cluster, because only the cluster's authoritative reporter writes them. These are the same rows the per-instance data source of the same name serves -- that one is how you reach a cluster from a host you already know, this one is how you enumerate a cluster you found through `fivenines_proxmox_clusters`. Reading it here needs no deduplication, and it does not go empty when one host's reporter ages out.

`status = "offline"` IS THE CLUSTER'S VIEW of a node, not ours: the surviving nodes cannot see it. That is the signal worth alerting on, and it is distinct from both "the agent stopped reporting" (`stale`) and "we cannot reach the Proxmox API at all" (the cluster's `unreachable_reporter_count`).

`stale` here is a FIXED 10-minute window -- not the organization threshold the guests data source uses.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fivenines_proxmox_clusters" "all" {}

# The nodes of one cluster, reached by cluster id rather than through a host you
# already know. Exactly one row per physical node however many hosts report the
# cluster: only the cluster's authoritative reporter writes them.
data "fivenines_proxmox_cluster_nodes" "prod" {
  cluster_id = one(data.fivenines_proxmox_clusters.all.proxmox_clusters[*].id)
}

# status = "offline" IS THE CLUSTER'S VIEW of a node -- the surviving nodes
# cannot see it. That is the signal worth alerting on, and it is distinct from
# both "the agent stopped reporting" (stale) and "we cannot reach the Proxmox
# API at all" (the cluster's unreachable_reporter_count).
output "offline_nodes" {
  value = [
    for n in data.fivenines_proxmox_cluster_nodes.prod.proxmox_cluster_nodes :
    n.name if n.status == "offline"
  ]
}

# `stale` here is a FIXED 10-minute window -- not the organization threshold the
# guests data source uses, so the same age can read stale there and fresh here.
data "fivenines_proxmox_cluster_nodes" "current" {
  cluster_id = one(data.fivenines_proxmox_clusters.all.proxmox_clusters[*].id)
  stale      = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) The Proxmox cluster's uuid -- `fivenines_proxmox_clusters`' `id`, NOT its `cluster_key`.

### Optional

- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the node name.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter over a fixed 10-minute window -- what the proxmox_node_status trigger reads, and not the organization threshold the guests data source uses. Omit for both.
- `status` (String) Filter by the cluster's view of the node. One of: `unknown`, `offline`, `online`.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `proxmox_cluster_nodes` (Attributes List) The rows the cluster's authoritative reporter wrote. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--proxmox_cluster_nodes))

<a id="nestedatt--proxmox_cluster_nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `proxmox_cluster_nodes`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `id` (String) Row identifier.
- `last_synced_at` (String) Server arrival time of the tick that last refreshed this row (never the agent's clock). Null when the row has never synced.
- `name` (String) The PVE node name, which IS that machine's system hostname -- the join key back to an instance.
- `proxmox_cluster_id` (String) The cluster these rows belong to. On this data source it is always the `cluster_id` you asked for; it is published so a row stays legible after rows from several clusters are merged.
- `stale` (Boolean) A FIXED 10-minute window, which is what the proxmox_node_status trigger reads -- NOT the organization threshold the guests endpoint uses. See ProxmoxGuest.stale.
- `status` (String) THE CLUSTER'S VIEW of this node, not ours. `offline` means the surviving nodes cannot see it -- the signal worth alerting on, and distinct from both "the agent stopped reporting" (`stale`) and "we cannot reach the Proxmox API at all" (the `collector` block). One of: `unknown`, `offline`, `online`.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
